name: OrigoDB
tagline: In-memory, command-sourced object database for .NET; superseded by its authors' Memstate rewrite.
description: OrigoDB is an in-memory database engine for .NET and Mono in which the entire data model is an ordinary object graph you define in C#. Every write is a serializable command object that is appended to a journal before being applied, so state is rebuilt on startup by replaying commands, optionally from a snapshot, which makes it an early, practical example of command sourcing applied to a database. Queries are LINQ or custom query objects run against the in-memory graph under a reader/writer lock, giving serializable ACID behaviour on a single node, with optional immutable models. Devrex Labs stopped development after 0.19.0 in December 2016 and points users to Memstate, a ground-up rewrite.
statusNote: No longer developed; last release 0.19.0 (Dec 2016). The authors recommend their rewrite, Memstate.

scale.notes: Whole data model must fit in RAM on one machine.

strengths: Domain model is plain C#, with no ORM or schema mapping
Command journal doubles as a full audit trail and allows point-in-time replay
Very fast reads because all data lives in process memory
weaknesses: Dataset limited by RAM, and startup replay time grows with the journal
Writes are serialized behind a single exclusive lock
useCases: Maintaining older .NET apps built on it
